subject: Temporary low-latency GPU slice for NimbleCart checkout pilot
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@nimblecart.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary low-latency GPU slice for NimbleCart checkout pilot

Team —

NimbleCart is ready to run a 7‑day pilot starting Monday 2026-06-28 focused on an extremely latency-sensitive checkout path. Product metrics and commercial context below; they need a predictable dedicated lane (not best-effort autoscale) to validate end‑to‑end p95 latency and SLOs for conversion impact.

Why this matters:
- Pilot is gated on checkout latency (p95 target <= 120ms).
- NimbleCart is a high-probability expansion: estimated ARR if pilot converts $120k/yr.
- They will route a production‑like traffic mix (burst QPS up to 45 qps, steady 12 qps) for 7 days.

Ask:
1) Temporary dedicated slice equivalent to ~4 A100 slots (or best perf-equivalent on our fleet) from 2026-06-28 00:00 UTC through 2026-07-05 23:59 UTC.
2) Autoscaling policy exception to prevent preemption during the window; ability to set a higher priority lane.
3) Reservation confirmation and an ops runbook (who to page if latency degrades).

I've attached the signed capacity request form from NimbleCart and a short note from legal on terms. We can accept cost on this POC (rev share or credit) but need a clear carveout.

Next steps: can someone confirm feasibility today? Also happy to jump on a 30-min sync with Ops/Infra this afternoon.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachments: nimblecart_capacity_request_form.pdf

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@nimblecart.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary low-latency GPU slice for NimbleCart checkout pilot

Laura —

Thanks for the clear ask and numbers. A few quick clarifying items before I lock anything in:
- Can you share a 48‑hour sample trace or a small traffic replay we can run in staging? We need sequence length distribution and token-per-request to size KV cache and batching.
- Do you require persistent KV cache across requests (stateful session affinity)? That impacts node topology.
- Is the traffic TLS-terminated through us or passed through their CDN?

Operationally we have two immediate options: a) temporary dedicated slice (what you asked for) or b) prioritized autoscale lane with prefix caching and a reserved warm pool (cheaper but slightly less isolation). For a strict p95 <= 120ms I suspect full slice is safer.

I can provision a tentative slot and mark it as "pending" until we get the trace + legal signoff. If we proceed with a full carveout we'll need an SLA-exception sign-off from Product Ops (Kimberly) and the finance owner to accept the cost for the pilot window.

I can be on a call at 3:30pm PT to walk through options.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Capacity & Infrastructure Ops
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Temporary low-latency GPU slice for NimbleCart checkout pilot

Sean —

Thanks. Quick answers inline: 
- We've attached a 48‑hour replay and token histograms to the capacity request PDF. Typical request is 80–140 tokens, median 95, long tail < 350.
- No persistent KV beyond single-user session affinity; a per-request KV with warm cache should be ok.
- TLS is terminated at our edge (NimbleCart CDN) and they POST to our API — so we control transport.

Business note: NimbleCart needs a deterministic SLA for conversions; if we can hit their p95 target this week they will advance to a quarter-long pilot and commit reserved capacity (they asked us to estimate committed spend during the call).

I can put together a short replay run for staging by 2pm PT. We'd prefer the full carveout for confidence but understand cost sensitivity.

— Laura

Folks —

Given the conversion upside and the fact this is a short, bounded pilot I'm ok approving a temporary dedicated carveout with the following guardrails:
1) Cap: 4 A100-equivalent GPU slots for 2026-06-28 00:00 UTC through 2026-07-05 23:59 UTC.
2) Cost: Product to own pilot bill; finance and sales will reconcile conversion credits if the pilot converts.
3) Ops: Sean to prepare a runbook (health checks, escalation list) and a rollback plan if tail latency exceeds target for >30m.
4) Compliance: NimbleCart to sign the limited-data-handling addendum (attached).

Marcus — please create the reservation in the dedicated pool and attach the reservation ICS. Sean, loop in on the 3:30 sync to agree on runbook steps.

— Kimberly
Kimberly Park
VP, Product Operations
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

- Pool: dedicated-lowlatency-us-west-2
- Capacity: 4 A100-equivalent slots (reserved, pre-warmed)
- Window: 2026-06-28 00:00 UTC -> 2026-07-05 23:59 UTC
- Ops on-call: Marcus Lin (primary), Sean Gallagher (secondary) — paging runbook linked.
- Cost: charged to Product (Laura Bennett) for pilot window; finance will handle post-mortem billing.

Playbook & links:
https://redwood.app/drive/capacity-requests/DEAL-9142
